content.text:
Fixed. `tests/test_totals.py` now passes, along with the rest of the suite (5 tests in total).

The bug was in `to_cents` in `ledger/currency.py`. It used `int(amount * 100)`, which truncates floating-point error. For example, `19.99 * 100` evaluates to `1998.9999…`, which became 1998. That one rounding error caused all three failures: `test_subtotal_single`, `test_subtotal_qty` and `test_total_discount`.

`to_cents` now converts through `Decimal(str(amount))` and rounds half up to whole cents.

Because `str()` is applied to the amount, a float such as `19.99` is read as the decimal 19.99, not its binary approximation. Amounts with more than two decimal places are now rounded to the nearest cent, not truncated. I didn't check whether anything else relies on the old truncation. The only caller I saw was `Line.cents`.
